full_judgment:
2. It has been stated in the above application under section 561A of the Code that one Abdul Motaleb having no locus standi filed petition of complaint in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Dhaka alleging offence under sections 406/420/467/468/469/471/109/506 to the effect the accused fraudulently took Taka 1 crore and 11 lac from witness No. 4 namely, Baby CO Nehar Afruz, wife of Safiullah of 3/B Purana Paltan, Dhaka to sell 4 flats but subsequently in breach of trust fraudulently refused to deliver possession of 4 flats whereby committed cheating and also processed to have constructed 14-storied building on plot No 40 of CS khatian No 6860 ga falsely creating the said above CS khatian for the land. 

 3. It has been stated that petition of complaint filed by said Motaleb shows no prima facie materials for offence under sections 406/420 Penal Code and private complaint for offence under sections 467/468/469/471/109/506 will be unmaintainable under section 195(c) of the Code as said CS khatian No. 6860 ga was produced and marked Ext. 3(b) in civil suit being TS 31/66 in the Court of 6th Munsif, Dhaka filed by plaintiff including Dr Mohiuddin, subsequently vendor of accused petitioner No. 2 and his wife and the said suit was decreed on contest on 7-2-75 against Government whose Title Appeal No. 149/75 preferred against said decree was also dismissed on contest on 31-3-77. Accordingly, it has been prayed that the Rule should be made absolute. 

 4. State-opposite party filed counter-affidavit to contest the Rule stating that the petition of complaint at the instance of Abdul Motaleb for witness No. 4 will be maintainable as for cognizable offence anyone can set the matter in motion before law and also stating that petition of complaint discloses prima facie materials for offence under sections 406/420, Penal Code. It has been stated that latest report of ADC (Revenue) disclosed fact as to fraudulent creation of said CS khatian No. 6860 ga by the accused petitioner. 

 6. Learned Advocate for accused petitioners submits that in view of production and having marked Exhibit No. 3(b) of CS khatian No. 6860 ga in TS 31/66 in 6th Munsif Court, Dhaka by plaintiffs including Dr Mohiuddin from whom accused petitioners No. 2 and his wife purchased lands in dag No 40 of the said khatian and in view of contested decree of said suit No. 31/66 on 7-2-75 and TA 149/75 by Government having been dismissed on 13-3-77 on contest, private complaint under sections 467/468/469/471/109/506 against said CS khatian No. 6860 ga will be unmaintainable under section 195(c) of the Code. He argues that no prima facie materials for offence under sections 406/420 Penal Code were disclosed in paras 7 and 11 of the petition of complaint. He contends that proceeding can be quashed at any stage even during investigation if no prima facie materials for alleged offence appear from petition of complaint or from FIR. In such connection he relies on the decision reported in 28 DLR (AD) 38. 

 7. Learned Deputy Attorney-General in reply submits that during investigation of the case no order as to quashment under section 561A can be legally passed. In such regard he relies on the decisions reported in 36 DLR (AD) 15, 26 DLR (AD) 17, 28 DLR (AD) 38, 1997 BLD (AD) 44. He refers to provisions of section 195(c) and contends that the bar will be operative against those who were party to the civil proceeding. Since the witness No. 4 of the petition of complaint was not party to the civil proceeding in which said khatian was filed as above private complaint under section 195(c) of the Code cannot be tenable. He contends that latest report of ADC (Revenue) discloses doubt as to existence of said CS khatian No. 6860 ga. He submits that in any view when all above matters are now within the domain of investigation agency no order as to quashment of the proceeding under section 561A of the Code will be tenable. He contends that the Rule must be discharged. 

 9. When admittedly the offences as alleged in the petition of complaint, treated as FIR by Ramna PS wherein PS case No. 30 dated 8-11-2002 was started, have been now under investigation by CID police, prayer for quashment under section 561A of the Code cannot be tenable in view of decisions cited above. It is now within the domain of the investigation agency to verify and see whether prima facie materials for offences as alleged in the petition of complaint are existing or not. If during investigation police finds no prima facie materials in support of offences as alleged in the petition of complaint, final report will follow and if prima facie materials be available charge-sheet will be submitted. When the matter is within the domain of the investigation agency it will be improper for the court to say any thing on the point inasmuch as Court process will only commence after submission of charge-sheet under section 173 of the Code by the police. It is also for the investigation agency to see whether offences as alleged under sections 467/468/469/471/109/506 will be tenable or not in view of section 195(c) of the Code due to production and being marked as Exhibit 3(b) of CS khatian No. 6860 ga in earlier civil suit (TS 31/66). This Court at this stage should not say anything as to existence or no existence of prima facie materials of the offences as alleged in petition of complaint in special view of the fact that the matter is admittedly under investigation of the CID police.
